newsitem.title: USA: Destron Fearing sees profit for FY97.
newsitem.headline: Destron Fearing sees profit for FY97.

text.p: Destron Fearing Corp said Wednesday that it expects to return to profitability in fiscal 1997.

The company on Wednesday reported a loss for fiscal 1996, ended September 30, of $0.33 a share, compared with a profit in fiscal 1995 of $0.06. The fiscal 1996 results included a $1.2 million write-off related to microchip readers and $1.2 million in legal fees for a successful patent suit.
"We expect to restore Destron Fearing to profitability for the fiscal year 1997," Randolph Geissler, president, said in a statement.
Destron Fearing manufactures electronic and visual identification devices for companion animals, livestock, laboratory animals, fish and wildlife.
"We have pioneered the development of animal ID markets and aligned ourselves with strong marketing partners," Geissler said.

Overseas markets, in particular, are growing rapidly, driven by government-mandated programs. There are 37 million dogs and 30 million cats in Europe, for example, and most European countries require permanent identification, he added.
Additionally, recent fears in Europe about the spread of "mad cow disease" may lead to electronic identification of animals.

"The European Commission has taken the position that all farm animals should be electronically identified by the year 2000 and plans to begin a million-animal trial in 1997," Geissler said. "Europe has 107 million cattle, 168 million hogs, and 130 million sheep. We are involved in a pilot program in the private sector, and we expect that market to expand in 1997."
Geissler said Destron also has shipped its first product to Japan where the products are being introduced this week.
In the United States, Destron has implant approvals for herd animals and has begun working with large cattle and hog producers, he added.
